title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. L is a set and Phi, Psi are 'admissible' families of subsets of L. Write |Phi| for the support (the union of the members). Admissible means two things. First, every x in |Phi| has a smallest member A(x) of Phi containing it. Second, no member A equals the union of the members strictly contained in it. Equivalently, every A is A(x) for some x. Such a family induces two structures on |Phi|. One is an equivalence relation, x ~ y iff A(x) = A(y). Its classes are the 'open strata' A^0 = A minus the union of the members strictly inside A. The other is a partial order on these classes. In the finite case this is exactly a finite T0 Alexandrov space, or a 'closed-cell' presentation of a stratified set. A subfamily Phi' of Phi is 'closed' if it is downward closed (B in Phi, B contained in A in Phi' implies B in Phi'). The notes say 'saturated' for subsets of |Phi| that are unions of strata.

The theorem in progress (pp. 7-9) shows that several conditions are equivalent; only (c) can be read here. Condition (a): Phi union Psi is admissible, and Phi and Psi are both closed subfamilies of it. Condition (c): |Phi| intersected with |Psi| equals |Phi intersect Psi|, and Phi intersect Psi is closed in Phi and in Psi.

The proof of (c) implies (a) occupies the previous page and the top of this one. The previous page shows the union is admissible, using the smallest elements A(x) and B(x). This page finishes as follows. By symmetry it suffices to show Phi is closed in Phi union Psi. Take A in Phi, B in Psi, B contained in A. Then B lies in |Phi| intersect |Psi| = |Phi intersect Psi|. Closedness of Phi intersect Psi in Psi gives B in Phi intersect Psi, hence B in Phi.

Definition: Phi and Psi are 'compatible' when these conditions hold. This is the combinatorial analogue of two cell complexes glued along a common subcomplex: both are subcomplexes of their union.

Corollary 1. If Phi and Psi are compatible, then |Phi| intersect |Psi| is saturated in |Phi| and in |Psi|, and the two equivalence relations (stratifications) it inherits coincide.

Warning. That last condition does not imply compatibility. Take Phi and the family Phi^0 of its open strata A^0. They have the same support and the same equivalence relation. But Phi^0 consists of pairwise disjoint sets. Compatibility would force each A^0 to lie in Phi and each A to lie in Phi^0, so the two families are compatible only if they are equal. In other words, the incidence order matters, not just the partition.

Corollary 2. If Phi and Psi are compatible, then |Phi| is contained in |Psi| iff Phi is contained in Psi, and |Phi| = |Psi| iff Phi = Psi. The next page justifies this by reducing to admissible subfamilies of the single admissible family Phi union Psi. That page then orders the set F(L) of admissible families by 'closed subfamily' and studies bounded sups, building toward an 'algebra of figures' (a lattice-like structure of compatible figures).
errors: Corollary 1 as transcribed says 'une partie de Psi qui est Psi-saturée'; it should read 'une partie de |Psi|' (slip of notation).

Minor: in step 2 the deduction B in Phi intersect Psi uses closedness of Phi intersect Psi in Psi together with |Phi intersect Psi| = |Phi| intersect |Psi|. The written line 'B in Phi => B in Psi' reads garbled or reversed; the intended conclusion is B in Phi. This is not a mathematical error.

In the counterexample the parenthetical justification is abandoned mid-sentence (struck-out lines). The claim itself is correct: closedness of Phi^0 in the union forces every A in Phi to lie in Phi^0, and vice versa, so Phi = Phi^0, i.e. every member equals its own open stratum (the members are pairwise disjoint).

ideas.what: Admissible families of subsets (smallest member containing each point; no member is the union of smaller ones) and their associated stratification into open strata A^0
ideas.modern_name: Finite T0 Alexandrov spaces / face posets of regular cell structures; closed-cell presentation of a stratified set
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandroff (1937) for finite spaces; McCord, Stong (1966) for finite spaces and posets
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the 'géométrie élémentaire / figures' themes; no known published version

ideas.what: Compatibility of two admissible families: the union is admissible and both are closed subfamilies; equivalently the intersection of supports is the support of the intersection, which is closed in both
ideas.modern_name: Gluing of finite spaces / cell complexes along a common closed subcomplex (pushout of closed embeddings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (CW and simplicial complexes; finite topological spaces)

ideas.what: Agreement of the induced partitions on the overlap does not suffice for compatibility (counterexample: Phi versus its family of open strata Phi^0)
ideas.modern_name: A stratification alone does not determine a cell or closure structure; the incidence (closure) order matters

ideas.what: For compatible families, support inclusion is equivalent to subfamily inclusion
ideas.modern_name: Closed subcomplexes are determined by their underlying sets

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary combinatorics of closure-type set systems (finite Alexandrov spaces, gluing along closed subfamilies). It is standard in substance. Its only interest is as a building block of the unpublished 1986 'algèbre des figures' project, and nothing on this page goes beyond folklore.
